title: On-call Capability Growth & Incident Education Roadmap
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines a 24-month roadmap to grow on-call capability across Redwood teams and formalize incident education for first responders, incident commanders, and stakeholders. It couples procedural runbook hygiene, a game-day syllabus, a repeatable post‑incident learning flow, and status/CSR messaging templates. The intent is to reduce detection-to-fix time, improve post-incident learning velocity, and scale on-call readiness without increasing operational headcount.

Scope

- Applicable teams: infra, serving-runtime, platform, eng-sre, eng-private-deployments, customer-success on escalation paths.
- Includes: runbook quality baseline, rotation design, continuous training (game-days), postmortem practice, status-page and customer message templates, measurable capability metrics.
- Excludes: vendor-managed incidents (follow vendor SLA playbooks) and feature-launch rollouts (handled by product launch checklist).

Principles

1. Evidence-first: every incident must surface measurable indicators (metrics, traces, logs) before escalation.
2. Small ROE (rules of engagement): responders act within defined scope—minimize blast radius.
3. Learn fast, ship small: convert postmortem findings into prioritized small improvements within 30 days.
4. Repeatable practice: quarterly game-days for all responder cohorts.

Key Objectives (KPIs)

- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) target: <= 2 minutes for P0 alerts.
- Mean time to restore (MTTR) target: improve by 30% across 12 months.
- Runbook coverage: >= 95% of critical services have updated runbooks tagged with last-reviewed <= 6 months.
- Postmortem action close rate: 80% of P0 actions closed or verified within 90 days.

Roadmap (high level)

Phase 0 (0–3 months): Runbook Triage and Baseline
- Inventorize all production runbooks and tag owners.
- Score runbooks by: accuracy (can reproduce), clarity (steps < 10), observability links (metrics/alerts/log links present), rollback options.
- Targets: 60% of critical runbooks pass minimum score.

Phase 1 (3–9 months): Training and Rotation Hygiene
- Implement a standardized rotation template (see section below).
- Launch onboarding module: 4-hour on-call fundamentals + sandboxes for new responders.
- Run monthly focused game-days (one service vertical per month).

Phase 2 (9–18 months): Incident Commander and Stakeholder Playbook
- Create IC training (decision ladders, comm cadence, postmortem facilitation).
- Harden status page templates and CSR messaging library.
- Establish a canary incident run (simulate multi-region failover) every 6 months.

Phase 3 (18–24 months): Automation and Competency Certification
- Integrate runbook actions into automation catalog (approved scripts, safe remediations).
- Offer competency badges based on simulation performance (Responder, IC, Bridge Lead).
- Measure confidence with periodic surveys and simulate escalation under load.

Runbook Hygiene Checklist (per service)

| Item | Owner | Cadence | Acceptable value | Notes |
|------|-------|---------|------------------|-------|
| Primary runbook URL | service-owner | every 90d | non-empty | link to playbook canonical page |
| Top-level impact classification | SLO-owner | every 90d | P0/P1/P2 defined | ties to SLO tiers |
| Alert-to-rollback procedure | oncall-owner | every 180d | tested | include CLI snippets |
| Observability links (dashboards/traces) | observability | every 90d | valid links | GUIDs for dashboards |
| Safety guardrails | security | annually | vetted | rollback approvals, kill-switch steps |

Sample Runbook: quick-patch-for-high-latency (text excerpt)

1) Detect: Confirm latency spike on /v1/generate (> 2s p95) using latency-dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/s/dash/latency-serviceX
2) Scope: Is impact region-specific? Check region metric panels (us-west-2, eu-west-1).
3) Mitigate:
   a) Enable traffic-weight routing to fallback model variant (Runtime CLI): redwood route set --service serviceX --model modelX‑fallback --weight 100
   b) If routing unavailable, scale up pool: redwood capacity scale --pool pool-serviceX --count +2
4) Verify: p95 latency returns below 1.5s within 5 minutes.
5) Post-incident: create postmortem PR with timeline and link to traces.

On-call Rotation Template

- Cadence options supported: weekly, biweekly, 7x24 primary + follow-the-sun secondary.
- Default: 7-day primary rotation with 48-hour shadow overlap for handoff.
- Minimum responders per rotation: 1 primary, 1 secondary, 1 bridge lead on call for P0s.

Example schedule snippet (ISO week IDs):
- Week 42: Primary = Alice M., Secondary = Ravi S., Bridge = Nora C.
- Week 43: Primary = Ravi S., Secondary = Alice M., Bridge = Evan B.

Escalation Matrix (short)

1. Primary responder receives alert (MTTA target 2m).
2. If unresolved after 10 minutes or if severity escalates to P0, summon secondary.
3. If unresolved after 20 minutes or cross-service impact, escalate to Bridge Lead and IC.
4. After 30 minutes of continued impact, notify Eng SRE manager and open operational bridge.

IC (Incident Commander) Playbook (quick guide)

- Immediate: confirm impact, assign roles (Scribe, Triage Lead, Mitigation Lead, Customer Comms).
- Communications: pin incident on #ops-bridge channel and set status page to "Investigating" within 15 minutes.
- Decision cadence: 15/30/60-minute checkpoints until mitigation.
- Evidence collection: collect representative traces, sample logs, and timeline entries in the running doc.
- Post-incident: ensure RCA draft exists before the incident is closed.

Postmortem Template (to copy into PR/Doc)

- Title: [DATE] [SERVICE] P0 - short title
- Summary: 3-line executive summary (who, what, impact).
- Severity & duration: start, mitigation time, resolution time, customer impact (requests affected).
- Timeline: bulletized with timestamps and actor initials.
- Root cause: evidence-backed explanation.
- Contributing factors: environmental, process, human, tooling.
- Remediation & action items: owner, due date, verification steps.
- Learning: changes to runbook, tests added, training required.
- Verified-by: IC and service owner signatures (names).

Game Day (quarterly syllabus)

Objective: validate runbooks, verify automation, assess cross-team coordination under controlled pressure.

Structure (4 hours):
- 0:00–0:30: Briefing & rules of engagement.
- 0:30–1:30: Simulated alert injection (single-service P1 escalates to P0).
- 1:30–2:30: Cross-region failover (introduce noisy neighbor).
- 2:30–3:15: Customer comms simulation & status page update exercise.
- 3:15–4:00: Retro and action assignment.

Success criteria: key runbook steps executed without prompts 80% of the time, status page updated within 15 minutes, automation runbook scripts executed without manual correction.

Evidence collection and scoring rubric:

- Detection: 0–5 points (alert fired & routed correctly).
- Acknowledgement: 0–5 points (MTTA in target).
- Mitigation: 0–10 points (appropriate steps executed).
- Communication: 0–5 points (status & CSR templates used).
- Post-event actions: 0–5 points (clear owners & due dates).

Status Page & CSR Messaging Library (templates)

- Investigating (internal & public):
  "We are aware of elevated latency for the generation API (region: {region}). Our team is investigating and will provide updates every 15 minutes. Impact: some requests may time out."

- Identified:
  "Root cause identified: {short cause}. We have applied a mitigation (routing to fallback model / scaling). Users should see degraded behavior improving; full remediation is ongoing."

- Mitigated / Partial Restore:
  "Mitigation in place. Most customers are seeing restored performance. We are continuing verification and working on a full fix. Follow-up: postmortem to be published within 5 business days."

- Resolved:
  "Issue resolved. The service is operating within normal parameters. A post-incident summary will be published with timelines and actions."

Customer-facing email snippet (P0, high impact)

Subject: Incident [INC-{id}] — Service Degradation Resolved

Hello {CustomerName},

We experienced a service disruption affecting {service} between {start} and {end}. We routed traffic to a fallback model and completed a full remediation. We will share a post-incident summary and any customer-impact rollups in the next 5 business days. If you observed data loss or billing anomalies, reply to this message and we will escalate immediately.

Thank you for your patience,
The Redwood Inference Operations Team

Roles & Ownership

- On-call roster owner: eng-sre (primary contact: eng-sre-rotations@redwood.internal).
- Incident commander playbook owner: eng-platform.
- Runbook review cadence owner: service owners (quarterly) coordinated by observability.
- Game-day coordinator: eng-learning.

Automation & Safe Playbooks

- Approved scripts must be stored in /automation/catalog and require a schema-validated metadata file before being added to runbooks.
- Each automated remediation must include a manual abort step and a rollback command.

Governance & Continuous Improvement

- Runbook audit: monthly sampling of 10% of critical runbooks; results reported to SRE leadership.
- Postmortem review board: monthly meeting to triage actions that require org-level changes.
- Quarterly competency report: aggregated game-day scores, MTTR trends, and completion rates for action items.

Appendix: Quick CLI Snippets

- Open bridge and annotate: redwood ops bridge open --service serviceX --severity P0 --note "opening bridge for latency spike"
- Route traffic to fallback model: redwood route set --service serviceX --model modelX-fallback --weight 100
- Scale capacity safely: redwood capacity request --pool pool-serviceX --delta 2 --reason "incident mitigation"

FAQ (short)

Q: Who should author a postmortem?
A: The IC and service owner jointly draft the postmortem; the IC owns timeline accuracy and the service owner owns root cause statements.

Q: What qualifies as a game-day failure?
A: Any event where runbook steps require >2 manual prompts or status page update misses 1 or more checkpoints.

Next steps (actions for Q1 after publication)

- Run initial inventory and scorecards (owner: eng-sre) — due 2025-11-30.
- Publish standardized rotation template and integrate into payroll/roster tool — due 2025-12-15.
- Schedule first cross-team game-day and invite observers (eng-learning) — due 2026-01-15.
